newsitem.title: FRANCE: Twenty-seven hurt as riverboat hits Paris bridge.
newsitem.headline: Twenty-seven hurt as riverboat hits Paris bridge.

text.p: A boat cruising along the Seine River hit a buttress of the historic Pont Neuf bridge in Paris on Monday, injuring 27 tourists on board but leaving the bridge undamaged, rescue workers said.
Most of the injured suffered only bruises or were simply shaken up and were quickly released after health checks at Paris hospitals.
But at least one person was in serious condition after suffering a blow to the chest in the accident, rescue workers said.
No one fell into the river. More than 80 rescue workers including divers quickly converged on the site following the accident to assure that no passengers had fallen overboard.
Police have opened an investigation into the cause of the accident, which took place on a clear and sunny day.
Eric Levavasseur, chairman of the boating company Vedettes du Pont-Neuf, owner of the riverboat Parisis, blamed it on an electrical failure in the system controlling the boat's rudder.
The Pont Neuf, built between 1578 and 1605, is the longest and oldest bridge spanning the Seine in the heart of the French capital. It is now undergoing restoration.
Dozens of riverboats ply the Seine, carrying more than 10,000 tourists a day past the city's historic sites.

The Pont Neuf links Paris' Right and Left banks to the Ile de la Cite, an island in the middle of the Seine where the famed Notre Dame cathedral, the main city police headquarters and law courts are located.
